citation: Grumbach K, Duffy CMC, Etz RS. Primary Care Clinician Uptake of Medicare Advanced Primary Care Management Billing Codes. J Gen Intern Med. doi:10.1007/s11606-026-10949-8
data: National survey of primary care clinicians
relevance_to_this_project: Survey complement: self-reported APCM use about 15% roughly a year after launch, and many clinicians unaware of the codes. This project adds national claims-based readiness and where QMB patients get care

citation: Informing Advanced Primary Care Management: Trends From Care Coordination Among Medicare Beneficiaries in 2020-2023. Perm J. 2025. doi:10.7812/TPP/25.040 (PMID 40820492)
reason: Pre-APCM CCM/PCM/TCM trends framed as groundwork for APCM
relevance_to_this_project: Pooled care coordination services (25.3M, $2.26B, 87% in physician offices); TCM under 20% and CCM under 5% of eligible patients. Consistent with this project's 2019-2024 trend

citation: Agarwal SD, Barnett ML, Souza J, Landon BE. Adoption of Medicare's Transitional Care Management and Chronic Care Management Codes in Primary Care. JAMA. 2018;320(24):2596-2597
reason: Baseline adoption of predecessor codes by primary care practices
relevance_to_this_project: 6.9% of practices with primary care physicians billed any CCM by 2016 and 21.5% any TCM; CCM reached 2.3% of eligible beneficiaries

citation: Agarwal SD, Barnett ML, Souza J, Landon BE. Medicare's Care Management Codes Might Not Support Primary Care As Expected. Health Aff. doi:10.1377/hlthaff.2019.00329
relevance_to_this_project: Larger practices and practices using other new codes adopted CCM/TCM first; about a quarter of CCM claims came from a practice other than the patient's assigned primary care practice. Supports using practice size and prior new-code use as forecast features

citation: ASPE. Analysis of 2019 Medicare FFS Claims for CCM and TCM Services: Descriptive Analysis. aspe.hhs.gov
